bull_case: Positive FCF can scale quickly if data economics dominate hardware investment over time.
bear_case: Satellite capex and SBC/ATM issuance may consume much of enterprise growth before it reaches each share.
thesis: Reinvestment runway is substantial, but per-share FCF quality is not yet Compounder-grade. FY2026 and H1 FY2027 cash flow improved sharply, while capex, SBC and equity issuance remain high relative to current revenue.

evidence.claim: FY2026 OCF was +$134.362M with PP&E purchases of $76.714M.
H1 SBC was $33.521M and Q2 ATM issuance raised about $122.4M.

counterevidence: Satellite services can raise revenue growth while also increasing hardware, launch and execution intensity versus pure imagery subscriptions.
unknowns: Normalized satellite-services gross margin, long-run owner FCF/share, and customer concentration after current sovereign contract ramp.
falsifiers: If NDR falls below 100%, RPO/backlog contract materially, or owner FCF/share turns persistently negative despite revenue growth, the thesis is downgraded.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Incremental returns are not proven exceptional, but structural collapse below cost of capital is not established.
Dilution is material and monitored, but the exact veto requires long-duration excessive dilution; the present evidence is serious but not yet enough for a hard veto.

next_checks: Next 10-Q: revenue mix, RPO/backlog, NDR, adjusted FCF, SBC, ATM issuance and capex

subscores.rationale: Revenue growth and recent positive FCF show improving returns, but cohort ROIC is not yet mature.
AI analytics, Pelican/Tanager and sovereign services offer a long runway, but require material capex.
FCF turned positive, yet SBC and equity issuance dilute per-share conversion.

uncertainties.rationale: Rapid business-model mix shift and early profitability make long-run normalization uncertain.
